items.title: Beyond religion and atheism: The secret third answer to big questions
items.description:
For decades, atheists have used one move to dismantle the case for God: swap in an evil one and show that the arguments work just as well. Philosopher Jack Symes was convinced by it, and was 50,000 words into a book defending atheism when he noticed that the exercise kept tipping toward goodness. He threw out the manuscript and started over. 
 
 This video  Beyond religion and atheism: The secret third answer to big questions  is featured on  Big Think .

items.title: Reading habits for the new literary ‘dark ages’
items.description:
The 18th-century writer and polymath Samuel Johnson was seldom seen without a book. People say he read in bed and while walking. He even read at dinner, the pages folded over his lap like a “dog who holds a bone in his paws in reserve while he eats something else,” as his biographer, James Boswell,  put it .

items.title: AI won’t replace biologists — it’ll just join the staff
items.description: Jennifer Doudna, Nobel Prize winner, biochemist, and CRISPR co-inventor, breaks down how AI is already reshaping experimental biology: speeding up mundane tasks like data cleanup and formatting, and increasingly helping spot patterns in large datasets that would be nearly impossible to catch by hand. items.title: Mercury lost its crown, and isn’t our Solar System’s hottest planet
items.description: In terms of power, the only body of note in the Solar System is the Sun. Planets, in general, reflect, absorb, and re-radiate energy emitted by their parent stars, and the Sun is the only parent star any of the planets have here in our Solar System. To an excellent approximation, the Sun keeps not only Earth, but all the planets at a temperature well above what they’d be without it, which is just a few Kelvin.
